 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• The longest highway in India is NH-44 (formerly known as NH-7), which runs from Srinagar in Jammu and Kashmir to Kanyakumari in Tamil Nadu, covering a distance of 3,745 km.
 
• NH-44 is the longest national highway in India, spanning a distance of 3,745 km.
 
• It was formerly known as NH-7 and is a part of the Golden Quadrilateral project, which aims to connect major cities in India with four-lane highways.
 
• The highway starts from Srinagar in Jammu and Kashmir and ends at Kanyakumari in Tamil Nadu.
 
• NH-44 passes through 11 states and connects several major cities such as Jalandhar, Delhi, Jaipur, Ahmedabad, Hyderabad, Bangalore, and Madurai.
 
• It also passes through important tourist destinations such as Agra, Khajuraho, and Hampi.
 
• The highway has been widened and upgraded to four lanes in several sections to improve connectivity and reduce travel time.
 
• NH-44 is a major lifeline for transportation of goods and people across India and plays a crucial role in India's economy.
 
• The highway is also known for its scenic beauty, passing through several mountain ranges, rivers, and forests, making it a popular route for road trips and tourism.
 
• NH-44 is a crucial link in India's road network, providing connectivity to several important ports, airports, and railway stations, and facilitating trade and commerce between different regions of India
